title: Optimal Segment-Routing Path Computation in PHP: Amortized Complexity and Invariant Guarantees
topic: The Complexity of Traffic Engineering in Segment Routing Networks
author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: Segment-routing networks enable flexible traffic engineering by encoding paths as ordered lists of segments. In this work we present a PHP-based implementation that computes all-pairs shortest paths with Floyd-Warshall and then selects optimal segment lists under a bounded segment budget. We analyze the algorithmic complexity, prove an optimal-substructure invariant, and evaluate the implementation on a single-core Xeon 6975P host. Empirical measurements show a mean latency of 29 584.82 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 33 801 ops/s over 30 iterations. The study demonstrates that a high-level language can deliver predictable traffic-engineering performance when algorithmic invariants are rigorously maintained. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261116_150240_the_complexity_of_traffic_engi}
